title: Confirm/decline/cancel a booking directly from the schedule calendar's detail popup
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- no backend change, the confirm/decline/cancel API this needs already exists (tasks 002, 016) and is already used by AdminDashboard.tsx's list view
keyConstraints: No backend work: POST /bookings/:id/confirm, POST /bookings/:id/decline, and POST /admin/bookings/:id/cancel already exist and are already called from frontend/src/api/client.ts's confirmBooking(id), declineBooking(id, reason?), and cancelBookingAsAdmin(id, reason?) -- these three functions must be reused as-, not reimplemented or duplicated. AdminCalendar.tsx (tasks 018/020) currently shows a booking's detail popup (role='dialog' aria-label='Booking details') as view-only -- a Close button only. This task removes that v1 limitation by adding the same Confirm/Decline/Cancel actions the list view already has (frontend/src/pages/AdminDashboard.tsx's handleConfirm/handleDecline/handleCancel), inside that existing popup, rather than building a second, separate action surface. AdminCalendar owns its own independent bookings fetch/state (established isolation pattern from tasks 018-021, does not share state with AdminDashboard's list) -- action handlers here must update AdminCalendar's own local state on success, the same way applyBookingUpdate does in AdminDashboard.tsx, not assume the list view's state exists or try to synchronize the two. A booking that becomes 'cancelled' (via decline or cancel) must disappear from the calendar grid on success, consistent with the existing client-side filter that already excludes cancelled bookings (AdminCalendar.tsx: bookings.filter((booking) => booking.status !== 'cancelled')) -- no new filtering logic needed, just make sure the local state update feeds that existing filter correctly. This must work in both View mode and Manage-availability mode (task 020) -- onSelectEvent already branches on event.kind so a booking tap behaves identically in either mode; do not gate these new actions behind view mode.
description: Extend AdminCalendar's existing booking detail popup with the same Confirm/Decline/Cancel actions already available in the list view (AdminDashboard.tsx), so the masseur can act on a booking directly from the calendar without switching views. Pending bookings get a Confirm button (immediate, single-tap, matching the list view) and a Decline button that reveals an optional-reason textarea before submitting (matching the list view's reveal-then-confirm pattern exactly). Confirmed bookings get a Cancel booking button with the same reveal-optional-reason-then-confirm pattern the list view already uses for masseur-initiated cancellation (task 016). On success, the popup closes (or updates to reflect the new status) and the calendar grid reflects the change immediately -- a confirmed booking turns from the pending color to the confirmed color; a declined or cancelled booking disappears from the grid.
acceptanceCriteria: Tapping a pending booking's calendar event and opening its detail popup shows a Confirm button and a Decline button, matching the list view's conditional rendering (status === 'pending')
Confirm is a single immediate action (POST via the existing confirmBooking(id)) -- on success the event's color/style updates to the confirmed style without a full recalendar refetch
Decline reveals an optional-reason textarea and a submit/cancel pair before calling the existing declineBooking(id, reason?) -- matches the list view's UX exactly, not a new interaction pattern
Tapping a confirmed booking's calendar event shows a Cancel booking button with the same reveal-optional-reason-then-confirm pattern, calling the existing cancelBookingAsAdmin(id, reason?)
On successful decline or cancel, the booking's event disappears from the calendar grid (consistent with the existing cancelled-bookings filter) and the detail popup closes

A failed confirm/decline/cancel surfaces the backend's error message inline in the popup (same ApiError-message pattern used elsewhere), leaving the booking and its popup state unchanged so the masseur can retry
401 on any of these three calls triggers onSessionEnded(), matching the existing pattern used for the calendar's own data fetch
This works identically whether the calendar is in View mode or Manage-availability mode (task 020) -- no new mode-gating logic
The existing AdminCalendar test suite (View-mode rendering, Manage-mode block/unblock) continues to pass unmodified alongside the new tests
Layout and tap targets for the new buttons verified usable at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, consistent with the calendar's established mobile-first requirement
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/pages/AdminDashboard.tsx (existing handleConfirm/handleDecline/handleCancel + decliningId/declineReason/cancellingId/cancelReason state shape -- reference for the exact UX pattern to replicate)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.tsx (add the actions to the existing booking detail popup)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.css (styling for the new buttons/reason form within the popup)
frontend/test/AdminCalendar.test.tsx (extend -- existing tests must still pass)
securityConsiderations: None beyond what already governs these three routes (requireMasseurAuth + adminRateLimit, unchanged) -- this task adds no new API surface, only a second UI entry point to three already-reviewed mutations.
openQuestion: Should the confirm/decline/cancel handler logic (the handleX functions plus their associated reveal-a-reason-form local state) be extracted into a shared hook usable by both AdminDashboard.tsx and AdminCalendar.tsx, or should AdminCalendar get its own independent copy of that thin wiring around the same three API functions -- the same way both components already independently call getAdminBookings for their own separate fetches, per the isolation pattern established across tasks 018-021? A shared hook removes some duplication (three handler functions plus ~4 pieces of reveal-form state, each maybe 15-20 lines), but this codebase has consistently chosen per-view independence over shared state/hooks so far, and the two views' local state shapes are already different (a flat bookings array vs a calendar events array derived from it). Architect should weigh this explicitly and give a recommendation rather than defaulting silently either way.
